decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm approach to the mouse, raising and pitching downward with gradual elbow-up motion; left arm stays in its workspace.
Align the right gripper above the mouse, continuing the downward pitch; keep fingers open and inspect before closing.
Lower around the mouse and close the right gripper. Retention is still uncertain until a small lift is observed.
Lift the mouse and begin a short rightward transfer with the gripper fully closed; inspect that the mouse follows.
Mouse did not follow the lift. Reopen and recenter slightly farther back, then descend deeper for a second grasp.
Close deeper around the mouse body and make a small vertical retention test before transferring.
Transfer the apparently retained mouse toward the pad while maintaining closure and modest clearance.
Mouse visibly follows the right gripper. Move over the pad center and lower toward its surface, retaining the grasp.
Set the mouse down on the pad and open, then withdraw the right hand. Raise and orient the left hand for a two-handed keyboard push.
Move both hands toward the keyboard front edge without crossing; keep clearance while establishing a matched pushing orientation.
Position closed fingers just in front of the keyboard at two separated contact points, lowering gradually before a gentle push.
Lower closed fingertips to keyboard edge height, bring the right contact inward, and begin a slow forward push.
Keyboard has moved forward. Continue a gentle synchronized diagonal push toward the outlined frame, keeping both hands on their respective sides.
Finish the keyboard push with small rightward and forward corrections, stopping short of crossing the left hand into the right workspace.
Withdraw and open both hands after the keyboard push. Move the left arm toward the figurine while the right retracts on its own side.
Approach the figurine shoulders from the left workspace with open fingers. Ease the right arm back toward its origin.
Correct the left gripper laterally to center the figurine's shoulders, lower slightly, and close for a retention test.
Test figurine retention with a slow vertical lift, maintaining full closure and leaving the right arm at rest.
The figurine slipped rather than lifting. Reopen and recenter farther left over its shifted torso before attempting another grasp.
Lower around the centered upper torso, close fully, and test with a short lift; the figurine is rotated so retention remains uncertain.
Lift the figurine slowly with the left gripper closed, then make a small inward move to verify that its base follows.
The figurine again stayed on the table. Reopen and approach a deeper torso grasp rather than the sloped shoulder, with small lateral correction.
Relieve the shoulder contact, reposition the open jaws toward the nearer torso, then close without forcing the tracking residual.
Test the deeper torso grasp with a slow lift and a small inward translation while retaining full closure.
The figurine is not retained. Release and clear it, then approach the clock from above; return to the figurine with a different grasp afterward.
Move the left hand toward the clock with a nearly vertical grasp orientation, staying left of the midline and above the keyboard.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller increments, lowering while approaching the clock to preserve joint continuity.
Use a less vertical clock approach, lowering and tilting forward to avoid the joint-limit region while keeping the left hand left of center.
Center the open left fingers around the clock, advancing slightly and lowering at small increments to clear the keyboard.
Close on the clock and test retention while lifting diagonally back-left, relieving the near-limit arm posture.
Replan after the rejected lift with much smaller back-left increments and minimal rise, keeping the clock grasp closed.
Use submillimeter increments to leave the sensitive IK region without changing the grasp or elbow branch.
Release the unretained clock and ease the wrist toward a shallower approach while retracting; avoid the sensitive near-limit pose.
Try a small lower-and-retract motion at fixed orientation to recover continuity and open the gripper.
Open and settle at the observed pose before another small retreat; no compensation for rejected commands.
Try a small downward wrist pitch during the retreat to leave the singular region on the current elbow-up branch.
Retreat back-left with a forward wrist tilt and slight lowering, seeking clearance from the elbow joint-limit region without branch switching.
Scale the rejected retreat to one-eighth increments, increasing only after several accepted small steps.
Make one tiny rearward motion and dwell rather than accumulate near the sensitive arm configuration.
Try a small inward retreat with a less downward wrist angle to reduce reach, interleaving holds for tracking.
Probe the opposite, smaller wrist adjustment with intervening holds; the previous retreat was rejected without motion.
Isolate a small vertical adjustment with the hand open, avoiding further lateral accumulation near the IK boundary.
Lower slightly around the clock, close, and test a small back-left motion without lifting into the sensitive IK region.
Release the clock and keyboard contact, then use very small back-left/down increments to recover from the near-singular posture.
With the elbow now away from its limit, close around the clock and test a small leftward retreat without a large lift.
Adjust the clock approach from its left, angling the fingers toward the clock while keeping the wrist left of center; inspect alignment before closing.
Angle the fingers slightly farther toward the clock without moving the wrist across center, close, then retreat in very small back-left increments.
Reopen and align with the displaced clock near the shared center, using a shallower approach; right arm remains well separated.
Close around the now-centered clock and retreat left and back at constant height to leave the folded near-limit posture before lifting.
Replan the rejected retreat with submillimeter motion and a small downward pitch, preserving closure and the current elbow branch.
Retreat gradually back into the left workspace with the clock grasp closed, adding only a small lift to test whether it follows.
Clock was not retained. Clear the left arm back into its workspace and approach the now-right-side clock with the right hand.
Return the left arm toward home and bring the right gripper above the clock with a moderate downward angle.
Replan with smaller left-home increments and center the open right gripper above the clock, lowering and pitching for a top grasp.
Match the clock's rotated edges, advance the right fingers slightly around its body, and close before a small retention test.
Lift and retreat slightly with the right gripper fully closed, checking whether the clock stays between the fingers.
The clock slipped. Reopen and change to a vertical top grasp centered over its current position instead of the previous slanted contact.
Replan the interrupted approach with smaller translation only, lowering and centering over the clock without further rotation near the IK boundary.
Relieve the low contact by lifting and backing the wrist while making the approach shallower; align the open jaws around the upper clock body.
Advance the open fingers from the clock's near corner toward its body center, close, then perform only a short lift test.
The fingers are still above the clock. Reopen and descend vertically to surround its lower body before closing.
Lift the deeper clock grasp slowly and retreat clear of the keyboard, keeping closure until visual retention is established.
Clock slipped from the wide diagonal edges. Clear it and turn the gripper to grasp its thinner front-to-back dimension.
Approach vertically over the clock with the jaws now opening along its thinner dimension, keeping the left arm clear.
Avoid the near-folded IK region by keeping the wrist back and tilting the fingers toward the clock while lowering in small increments.
Center the thin-axis jaws farther around the clock and close, keeping the wrist angle and small approach increments.
Test the thin-axis clock grasp by lifting slowly back from the keyboard; watch for both clock retention and unintended keyboard contact.
Recenter over the clock's current body and descend with open jaws; the last lift showed it stayed on the table, so no retention is assumed.
Relieve keyboard contact and shift the thin-axis grasp farther around the clock body, then close at the observed height.
Test the newly centered thin-axis clock grasp with a slow back-and-up lift, maintaining full closure and checking RGB retention.
Move the apparently caught clock toward a central transfer position, keeping the right wrist on its side and inspecting whether the clock follows.
Clock now visibly follows the right hand. Bring it to the central front staging area for a left-arm transfer without crossing arms; raise the left hand clear.
Retention became ambiguous and the keyboard may have been contacted. Open and withdraw the right hand to obtain a clear view before further manipulation.
Clock is now in the central foreground. Clear the right arm to its side and approach with the left using a thin-axis grasp, keeping separation.
Approach the staged clock from the left with jaws along its depth, while returning the separated right arm toward home.
Center the left thin-axis jaws farther around the staged clock and close at its body height, keeping the right hand clear.
Test the centered left-hand clock grasp with a gradual up-and-left retreat, maintaining closure and watching for clock motion.
Clock slid instead of lifting. Reopen and descend substantially deeper around its current lower body for a more secure thin-axis grasp.
Lift and translate left with the deeper closed grasp, checking whether the clock moves with the fingers instead of sliding free.
Clock appears to have followed the deeper grasp. Lift and move left toward the drawer with closure maintained, checking retention during transfer.
